defaults.permitted_development: Across Buckinghamshire, boundary walls, fences and gates are usually permitted development if they stay no higher than 1 metre next to a highway used by vehicles and no higher than 2 metres elsewhere, or if an already-higher boundary is altered without increasing its height. That fallback can disappear where an Article 4 direction or an old planning condition has removed the normal householder right.

rules.height_rules: Across Buckinghamshire, for ordinary houses, most fence and wall questions come back to the same split between the 1 metre highway-side limit and the 2 metre limit elsewhere.
rules.depth_rules: Across Buckinghamshire, a wall or fence is not assessed like an extension. The key issues are usually where it sits and how high it is, rather than how thick it is.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Buckinghamshire, the same boundary treatment can be acceptable in one position and need permission in another once it fronts a road or sits on a prominent corner.
rules.roof_rules: Across Buckinghamshire, ordinary boundary rules do not create a roof allowance. Gate canopies or covered entrance features should be checked separately.
rules.materials_rules: Across Buckinghamshire, material choice is usually a design issue rather than a standalone permitted-development test, although listed-building and conservation-area contexts can make inappropriate boundary finishes much harder to defend.

restrictions.conservation_area: Boundary works in conservation areas are more sensitive because removal as well as replacement can affect the character and appearance of the area.
restrictions.listed_building: Historic boundary walls and railings are often part of a listed building's significance, so replacement or removal can need listed building consent.
restrictions.article4_notes: Article 4 directions and site-specific conditions are a common reason why an otherwise modest boundary change still needs planning permission.

rules.height_rules: For ordinary houses, most fence and wall questions come back to the same split between the 1 metre highway-side limit and the 2 metre limit elsewhere.
rules.depth_rules: Boundary can still need permission because of its position and visual impact even though there is no formal depth limit.
rules.boundary_rules: The same boundary treatment can be acceptable in one position and need permission in another once it fronts a road or sits on a prominent corner.
rules.roof_rules: Ordinary boundary rules do not create a roof allowance. Gate canopies or covered entrance features should be checked separately.
rules.materials_rules: National planning rules focus on height and siting rather than a fixed material list, but visible front boundaries should still use finishes that suit the house and street. Heritage areas are more demanding on detail.

restrictions.conservation_area: Conservation area status can tighten the position for boundary works, and separate consent may be needed to demolish an existing wall, fence or gate that contributes to the area's character.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building controls can apply to fences, gates and walls where they form part of the building's curtilage or historic setting.
restrictions.article4_notes: Do not rely on the normal 1 metre or 2 metre rule where Article 4 controls or earlier planning conditions remove those householder rights.
